44065727.article_content:
Suppose that you have an array of N elements and you want to divide it into M chunks. It is a common task when trying to spread N units of work over M threads, for example.
You want chunks to be all the same size, plus or minus one element (fair sized). It might be slightly harder than you imagine.
Following Python, wse the convention that a//b is the integer quotient so that 5//2 is 2. And let % be the ‘remainder’ : 5%2 is 1.
The naive algorithm uses the following chunk ranges: [0, N//M), [N/M, 2*N//M)… up to [N//M*M, N). Thus all chunks have size N/M but there is an extra chunk of size N%M.
If N is 5 and M is 2, we have the chunks [0,2), [2,4), [4,5).
That is not great. We have one extra chunk ! At least we do when N//M is at least one.
Instead, we can make the last chunk possibly larger. We use the ranges [0, N//M), [N/M, 2*N//M)… up to [N//M*(M-1), N). If N is 5 and M is 2, we have the chunks [0,2), [2,5). At least we have the right number of chunks.
But what if we have N is 20 and M is 6? We get the chunks [0,3), [3,6), [6,9), [9,12), [12,15), [15,20). It is quite bad because the last chunk is much larger.
Instead, you might try the following: let the chunk size be ceil(N/M). That is, the chunk size is N/M rounded up. Thus if N is 5 and M is 2, we have that the chunk size is ceil(5/3) or 3. We use the chunk ranges: [0, ceil(N/M)), [N/M, 2*ceil(N/M))…[(M-1)*ceil(N/M), N). If N is 5 and M is 2, we have the chunks [0,3), [3,5). That is much better. This time, we have the right number of chunks. One has size 3 and the other one has size 2. But if fails if N is 12 and M is 5. We get that the chunks size is 3, and so the ranges are [0,3), [3,6), [6,9), [9, 12). So we are missing one chunk!
So what should you do? A better approach is to have the first N%M chunks have size ceil(N/M) and have the remaining N-N%M chunks have size floor(N/M).
Let me implement it in Python. The get_chunk_range_simple function divides a total of N elements into M chunks and returns the start and end indices of the i-th chunk (0-indexed). It handles uneven divisions by distributing the remainder across chunks: the first remainder chunks (where remainder = N % M) have size quotient + 1 (where quotient = N // M), while the remaining chunks have size quotient. For a given chunk index i, the function calculates the start as quotient * i + min(i, remainder), accounting for the extra elements in earlier chunks, and the end as quotient * (i + 1) + min(i + 1, remainder), ensuring the range reflects the cumulative effect of previous chunk sizes. This approach ensures all elements are covered, with earlier chunks absorbing the remainder for balanced distribution.

,
M
,

44065727.article_summary:
本文讨论了如何将一个包含N个元素的数组公平地分成M个 chunk，使得每个 chunk 的大小尽可能均匀。常见的问题是当N不能被M整除时，会导致某些 chunk 多出一个元素。文章提出了几种算法：

1. **简单算法**：每个 chunk 大小为 N//M，剩余的元素形成一个额外的 chunk，但这会导致 chunk 数量不对或不均匀。
2. **改进算法**：将剩余元素分配到最后一个 chunk，使其可能更大。
3. **最佳算法**：前 N%M 个 chunk 大小为 ceil(N/M)，其余 chunk 大小为 floor(N/M)。这样可以均匀分配剩余元素。

文章提供了一个 Python 函数 `get_chunk_range_simple`，根据 chunk 索引 i 返回其起始和结束位置，确保 chunk 数量正确且分布均匀。类似的实现也可以用 C++ 完成。

例如，当 N=20，M=6 时，前 N%M 个 chunk 会比其他 chunk 多一个元素，从而实现公平分配。

data.title: Judges Shouldn't Rely on AI for the Ordinary Meaning of Text
data.author: hn_acker
data.article_summary:
文章讨论了大型语言模型（LLMs）在司法工作中的应用及其潜在问题。尽管有人建议利用LLMs解释法律文本的“通常意义”，但文章指出，这些模型并非中立的，它们反映了开发者的选择和利益，可能带有偏见和隐私风险。LLMs虽可辅助法官检索历史资料或法律 drafting，但不应成为解释法律意义的工具，否则可能导致司法解释权向私营公司转移。

美国和国际法院已开始关注LLMs的应用。美国第十一巡回上诉法院的Judge Kevin Newsom曾使用LLMs解释法律条款，而D.C.上诉法院在Ross v. United States案中对LLMs的态度存在分歧。一些国家如中国和巴西已将LLMs纳入司法流程，但出现如引用虚构判例的问题。

文章还指出，AI公司有能力操控LLM输出，通过技术手段如“Constitutional AI”引导模型响应，强调LLMs的透明性和责任性问题。总体而言，文章认为LLMs在司法中的应用需谨慎，以防其影响司法公正。

Justin  Curl
Peter  Henderson
Kart  Kandula
Faiz  Surani
Meet The Authors
Published by
The Lawfare Institute
in Cooperation With
Subscribe to Lawfare
Judges
are debating how large language models (LLMs) should fit into judicial work. One popular idea is to consult LLMs for the “ordinary meaning” of text, a key issue in statutory interpretation. At first glance, this may seem promising: These models, trained on massive amounts of human language, should reflect everyday usage.
Several
critiques
, however, have already highlighted technological flaws with this conception, including inaccuracies introduced by nonrepresentative training data and privacy risks posed by use of third-party artificial intelligence (AI) services.
But valid as these concerns are, they obscure a more fundamental issue: LLMs
embody the discretionary choices
of their creators, not the median of human language. Their responses are controlled by private entities, each with their own economic interests and ideological commitments. LLMs are powerful tools that will likely have many applications in the judiciary—for instance, retrieving historical materials relevant to determining meaning, or assisting with legal drafting. But they are not themselves neutral arbiters of ordinary meaning, and judges should not treat them as such. Relying on models in this way risks delegating core interpretive functions to actors with incentives to manipulate judicial outcomes. This transfer of influence to unaccountable private interests represents not merely a technical challenge requiring judicial caution, but a structural incompatibility with the judicial role.
Judges are already using AI to answer legal questions.
This concern about the privatization of legal interpretation is not merely theoretical—the integration of LLMs in judicial decision-making is already garnering significant attention in U.S. and international courts. Judge Kevin Newsom of the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit documented his experimentation with LLMs in two notable concurrences.
In the first case
, the court examined whether an insurance contract covering harms related to “landscaping” encompassed the installation of an in-ground trampoline.
In the second
, the court addressed whether a sentencing enhancement applicable to armed robberies involving “physical restraint” included situations where victims were threatened at gunpoint. In both cases, Judge Newsom consulted LLMs to assess their interpretation of these contested terms, ultimately expressing optimism about these technologies’ interpretive utility.
More recently, the District of Columbia Court of Appeals presented a microcosm of judicial attitudes toward LLMs through three divergent opinions in
Ross v. United States
. Writing for the court, Judge Vijay Shanker adopted a skeptical position, explicitly rejecting ChatGPT as a reliable determinant of common knowledge. By contrast, Judge John Howard’s concurrence expressed optimism regarding the judiciary’s potential integration of LLMs, contingent on addressing security and privacy concerns. Judge Joshua Deahl’s dissent went furthest, substantiating his legal position with ChatGPT’s outputs.
Some international jurisdictions have adopted more aggressive approaches to LLM implementation.
A court in China
has integrated LLMs into judicial workflows, with judges using these models to generate full opinions in civil and commercial cases. Similarly,
Brazil’s justice system
has deployed various AI tools to address its substantial case backlog. This rapid adoption has not been without complications, however, as evidenced by a Brazilian judicial decision drafted using ChatGPT that cited fabricated legal precedent.
LLM outputs are susceptible to intentional manipulation by AI companies.
AI labs have the commercial incentive and technical capability to modify the outputs of their models. Developers have various tools for intentionally altering an LLM’s outputs, including with prompt wrappers that encode values that guide outputs and explicit filters that prevent the model from responding to certain prompts. Both techniques are already in use in state-of-the-art AI systems.
For example, in late 2022 Anthropic introduced one method for intentionally altering an LLM’s outputs called
Constitutional AI
: a process for training an AI assistant that would abide by a “list of rules or principles” created by human beings. To promote transparency, Anthropic published the
full list of rules and principles
that it used to train its then state-of-the-art AI assistant. data.title: Ask HN: Do you have a side project you're getting tired of?
data.author: gdulli
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：处理和对待个人项目或副业项目的态度和方法

不同观点：
• RadiozRadioz认为，在项目初期快速原型设计和探索问题领域时充满激情，但一旦问题解决、路径明确后，剩下的实施工作会变得枯燥无味。他的大脑会自动寻找新的问题，而不是继续完成剩下的“按部就班”的任务。

• guywithahat指出，自己的副业项目通常没有社区参与，并建议那些寻找项目的人可以尝试联系那些已经停止更新但仍有待解决问题的老项目作者。

• achieve_freedom表示自己有一个曾赚到少量钱的iOS应用，但由于缺乏在特定领域的知识，无法有效营销。他更关注当前的新项目，并询问其他人具体在寻找什么样的项目。

• rasulkireev认为自己很幸运能够自托管项目，这样在厌倦一个项目时可以轻松停止，不必担心服务切换，因为所有基础设施都是自己搭建的，项目可以自主运行。

• whatamidoingyo直接询问是否有人打算购买项目，表现出对项目交易的兴趣。

• busymom0提到自己开发的一个生产力应用难以获得关注和下载，尽管进行了多次优化和推广尝试。她对是否放弃这个项目感到犹豫。

补充讨论：
• 项目厌倦感：RadiozRadioz描述了一种在解决问题后失去兴趣的心理现象，这可能是许多开发者在项目中后期遇到的常见问题。

• 项目营销与推广：busymom0和achieve_freedom都提到了项目营销的挑战，尤其是如何有效推广和吸引用户，这是许多独立开发者面临的难题。

• 项目社区与合作：guywithahat建议寻找有社区支持的项目，强调了社区在项目持续发展中的重要性。

• 项目自主性与可持续性：rasulkireev强调自托管项目的好处，即在项目完成后无需持续干预，能够自主运行，减轻了开发者的负担。

争议焦点：
• 项目的后期实施工作是否枯燥：RadiozRadioz认为项目后期的工作缺乏吸引力，而rasulkireev则表示如果项目能够自主运行，就可以轻松摆脱项目负担，暗示后期工作不一定是问题。这体现出开发者对项目不同阶段的感受和处理方式的差异。

data.author: zdw
data.article_summary: 文章《在临终之际，我只有一个遗憾：没有花更多时间重置密码》以幽默口吻讲述了一位老人在生命尽头对密码管理的反思。他一生成就辉煌，但唯独对未能投入更多时间创建和重置密码感到遗憾。他描述了现代生活对密码的依赖，以及每次重置密码带来的“成就感”。他批评年轻一代依赖密码管理器，认为这样缺乏牺牲精神。最终，他将自己的巨额财富留给了孙子，但前提是必须破解一系列复杂的密码和安全问题。文章以讽刺方式探讨了现代技术带来的烦恼和荒谬。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对垄断公司开发的低质量软件的抱怨和态度

不同观点：
• 观点一：有些人对垄断公司开发的低质量软件感到极度不满，认为这些公司不关心用户体验。例子：Sloppy提到在临终时仍然想抱怨这些公司制作的糟糕软件，显示出对这种情况的强烈沮丧和无力感。

On My Deathbed, I Have Just One Regret: Not Spending More Time Resetting Passwords
by
Lindsey Smith
Come closer, grandchild. Thanks for visiting me one last time before I die. I’ve lived a great life. I climbed Mt. Everest, founded a Fortune 500 company, and had six amazing children. But there’s one mistake that haunts me: not spending more of my life creating, entering, and re-entering passwords.
I’m ashamed to admit that for decades, I coasted by with a couple of passwords scribbled on a Post-it next to my laptop. That is, until websites started requiring passwords just to check the weather or read the news. Suddenly, I needed a login for everything. That’s when I realized: Nothing makes you feel more alive than registering for an account, making a password, instantly forgetting it, and repeating the whole process for every transaction. You haven’t really lived until you’ve reset a password four times just to peruse a forum on bathtub grout.
Some people say that no one on their deathbed ever said, “I wish I’d spent more time at work.” It’s true. I don’t wish I’d spent more time at work. I do wish I’d spent more time on the phone with IT while they authenticated my newly changed password on seven different devices. You know, if you do what you love, you’ll never work a day in your life. That’s why I’m so glad my company made us reset our passwords every three months.
Your generation is so entitled. You expect immediate success. Phooey! No one is born knowing how to create and remember scores of different sequences of digits, capitalized letters, and obscure symbols. Like any world-class craft, you must practice it for at least ten thousand hours. You have to make sacrifices. If you spend all your time with friends and family, you’ll never be lonely. But if you spend all your time practicing password entry, you’ll never be locked out of that pedometer app you’ve only used once.
No, the secret to success is delayed gratification. You know, a lot of nights on the couch while we were watching TV, your grandmother would beg me to turn it off and engage with her emotionally. But I would always turn her down. Sure, it’s satisfying to connect with your soulmate of fifty years. But using a remote control to type in a twelve-digit password one letter at a time is even more satisfying.
I worry about your future. The ice caps are melting, democracy is on the brink of collapse, and worst of all, passwords are being replaced with Touch ID. Without the constant need to remember and manually type nonsensical combinations of letters and numbers, you’ll have no choice but to do terrible things, like pay attention when someone talks to you.
That’s why I was so devastated when your uncle, my oldest child, told me his deepest, darkest secret. He’s been using an online password manager for the last five years. He doesn’t even type in the letters himself. It just auto-populates. That’s why I cut him out of my will.
Which brings me to why I’ve called you here today. I’m leaving you my fortune. You get the mansion, the beach house, and the yacht. But the greatest gift I’m leaving you is not the money. It’s a life without regrets. That’s why I’ve locked myself out of all my online accounts. You’ll need to figure out every password to access the funds. You’ll also need to correctly answer a dozen security questions, like the name of the street where I was conceived or my childhood best friend’s favorite movie. In fact, you’ll probably need to quit your job and dump your girlfriend.
Going forward, you’ll only have time to focus on life’s most important mission: resetting passwords. Godspeed, grandchild.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：SimStudio产品的功能、定位、用户体验及其与竞争对手的比较。

不同观点：
• [manish_sg] 关注SimStudio是否支持在SaaS中嵌入多租户部署。他认为这是一个关键问题，因为这涉及到产品的应用场景和适用性。

• [matt3D] 对编配工具的用户体验（UX）提出了批评，认为这些工具没有优先考虑人工智能（AI）特性。他建议工具的首要功能应是帮助用户通过提示窗口搭建编配流程。

• [jasongill] 提到了SimStudio在市场上的竞争，并与其他具有AI功能的编配工具（如n8n和Rivet）进行比较。他希望看到SimStudio的独特之处和优势。

• [srameshc] 提供了关于产品主页的反馈，认为当前主页不足以清晰传达产品功能，建议参考GitHub上的GIF演示来改进网站说明。

• [primitivesuave] 对SimStudio的发布表示祝贺，并对团队快速迭代产品的能力表示赞赏。他特别提到SimStudio在React Flow方面的优秀表现。

• [flaviuspopan] 对SimStudio表示兴趣，但提出了两个实际问题：一是关于未来的定价策略，二是关于MCP服务器集成的可能性，以支持特定的业务需求。

• [worldsayshi] 认为像Figma/Excalidraw那样的画布解决方案在不同的问题领域中具有潜力，暗示这种交互方式可能适用于更多场景。

• [barbazoo] 建议增加更多实际案例，以便用户更好地理解产品的应用场景。

• [efitz] 将SimStudio比喻为“IFTTT for LLM agents”，暗示其功能类似于IFTTT，但专注于LLM（大型语言模型）代理。

• [Geep5] 表达了对编配工具空间（如Rivet）的喜爱，尤其是开源和免费的特性，使其编码体验更加愉快。

补充讨论：
• 用户对SimStudio的功能、用户体验和市场定位存在不同关注点，有人关注其技术实现（如MCP服务器集成），有人关注其市场竞争力及定价策略。

主要讨论点：数学可视化、质数与合数的因式分解技巧、动画与交互改进建议

不同观点：
• hiAndrewQuinn：分享了一种通过检查2、3、5、7的倍数来快速分解100以内合数的方法，并举例说明如何应用于具体数字。该方法强调了在低数值范围内质数的普遍性以及因式分解的简便性。
• math_dandy：指出三的幂形成的图形类似于Sierpinski三角形，揭示了数学中的图形美。
• worldsayshi：对可视化工具表示赞赏，并提议开发一个拖放工具来动态展示数字因式分解的过程，同时询问这种可视化算法的名称。
• pvg：提供了一些旧的讨论链接，可能包含相关解释和讨论。
• glaucon：建议动画可以慢速或逐步播放，以便更好地观察数字的变化。
• kccqzy：同样建议放慢动画速度，并希望看到更清晰的圆圈添加过程。
• gavmor：对动画中数字顺序的正确性提出质疑，担心跳跃过于剧烈。
• jderick：建议将所有数字放在一页上，并允许缩放和过滤不同的因素或数字范围，以观察模式。
• mousethatroared：分享了个人故事，表达了对因式分解可视化的兴趣和实用性。
• dtjohnnymonkey：表示对高合数而非质数的兴趣。
• smusamashah：询问是否可以输入自己的数字来查看其图形表示。
• tocs3：对排列点的算法表示好奇。
• liendolucas：提议将此工具用于显示时钟的数字。
• carterschonwald：指出这种可视化方法可能是Brent Yorgey最初发明的。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中多次提到动画速度和交互性改进，反映了用户对更清晰和可控的可视化体验的需求。
• 有人对可视化算法的名称和具体实现表示好奇，显示出对数学图形背后的算法有深入了解的兴趣。
• 个人故事和实际应用建议（如用于教育或时钟显示）展示了该可视化工具的广泛吸引力和实用潜力。

data.title: By default, Signal doesn't recall
data.author: feross
data.article_summary: Signal Desktop引入了一项新的“屏幕安全”设置，旨在防止Windows系统上的电脑截取Signal聊天内容的截图，特别是在微软推出“Recall”功能后。Recall会定期截取用户屏幕并存储为可搜索的数据库。尽管微软在回应批评后对Recall做了调整，但它仍可能威胁隐私保护应用的安全。因此，Signal在Windows 11上默认启用了该保护设置，阻止截图功能，同时提供了可手动关闭的选项，但需要经过警告和确认步骤。Signal此举是为了在缺乏细化开发者工具的情况下保护用户隐私，同时呼吁AI开发团队在未来更慎重考虑隐私与可访问性之间的平衡。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Signal的Recall功能及其隐私和安全问题，涉及DRM、数据保护、以及用户对隐私设置的期望。

不同观点：
• **支持Signal的隐私保护措施**：一些用户（如vel0city）认为Signal对Recall功能的保护措施是合理的，尤其是Recall数据库的访问比Signal消息目录更难。同时，vel0city指出，如果攻击者能直接查询Recall数据库，他们很可能已经能够读取设备上的所有Signal消息，因此这种保护是有效的。

• **对元数据保留的担忧**：mmooss指出，虽然Signal有“消失消息”的功能，但该功能不适用于语音和视频通话记录，这些记录会保留在设备上，可能对用户隐私构成威胁，尤其是对人权活动人士等高风险用户。他们认为，Signal应该对所有数据和元数据提供统一的隐私设置，而不是区别对待。

• **对DRM的批评**：一些用户（如Peacefulz、contact9879、WD-42）对Signal需要使用DRM来保护用户数据感到不满，认为这是对用户自由的限制，尤其是当用户需要保护自己免受自己设备上的潜在威胁时。

• **对Windows和操作系统控制的讨论**：plingbang和compsciphd提到，操作系统始终对应用程序有控制权，应用程序只能请求操作系统执行操作。因此，Microsoft有可能修改Recall以捕获DRM标记的内容。此外，compsciphd认为，Signal消息历史以SQLite数据库的形式保存在设备上，本身也是一个隐私问题，因此仅关注Recall的保护可能只是表面功夫。

• **对Signal功能的期望**：kiririn希望Signal能提供将消息包含在iOS备份中的选项，而habitue则表达了对封闭源代码操作系统的普遍不信任，尤其是Microsoft。

补充讨论：
• **Recall功能的实际需求**：bcoates分享了使用Timesnapper（Recall的前身）的经验，认为该功能对于记录工作时间非常有用，并且与多模态LLM结合可能会更加有用。

• **技术实现的争议**：pseudosavant质疑Signal是否在填补一个早就应该解决的漏洞，而josephcsible则关注如何绕过Recall的限制以获取高质量的截图。

• **对Linux的推广**：godelski和enfuse在讨论中提到了Linux作为Windows和MacOS的替代方案，认为Linux的用户体验已经显著提升，并预测其用户群会继续增长。

争议的焦点：Signal使用DRM保护Recall功能是否必要，以及这种保护是否真正提升了用户的隐私安全，还是只是流于形式。同时，用户对Signal在不同类型数据上的隐私保护措施存在不满，尤其是元数据的保留问题。

By Default, Signal Doesn't Recall
jlund
on 21 May 2025
Signal Desktop now includes support for a new “Screen security” setting that is designed to help prevent your own computer from capturing screenshots of your Signal chats on Windows. This setting is automatically enabled by default in Signal Desktop on Windows 11.
If you’re wondering why we’re only implementing this on Windows right now, it’s because the purpose of this setting is to protect your Signal messages from
Microsoft Recall
.
First announced on May 20, 2024, Microsoft Recall takes screenshots of your apps every few seconds as you use your computer and then stores them in an easily searchable database. In Microsoft’s
own words
, its goal is to act as a sort of “photographic memory” for everything that you do on your computer. The words that other people chose to describe Recall upon its debut were decidedly less positive.
1
After an intense
security backlash
and significant public outcry, Microsoft quickly pulled the feature.
It’s a one-year anniversary that nobody wants to celebrate, but Recall
is back
and Signal is ready.
Although Microsoft made several adjustments over the past twelve months in response to critical feedback, the revamped version of Recall still places any content that’s displayed within privacy-preserving apps like Signal at risk. As a result, we are enabling an extra layer of protection by default on Windows 11 in order to help maintain the security of Signal Desktop on that platform even though it introduces some usability trade-offs. Microsoft has simply given us no other option.
Fade to Black
If you attempt to take a screenshot of Signal Desktop when screen security is enabled, nothing will appear. This limitation can be frustrating, but it might look familiar to you if you’ve ever had the audacity to try and take a screenshot of a movie or TV show on Windows. According to Microsoft’s
official developer documentation
, setting the correct
Digital Rights Management
(DRM) flag on the application window will ensure that “content won’t show up in Recall or any other screenshot application.” So that’s exactly what Signal Desktop is now doing on Windows 11 by default.
Apps like Signal have essentially no control over what content Recall is able to capture, and implementing “DRM” that works for you (not against you) is the best choice that we had. It’s like a scene in a movie where the villain has switched sides, and you can’t screenshot this one by default either.
Warning Shots
Microsoft has launched Recall without granular settings for app developers that would enable Signal to easily protect privacy, which is a glaring omission that limits our choices. Signal is using the tools that are available to us even though we recognize that there are many legitimate use cases where someone might need to take a screenshot. For example, some accessibility software (such as screen readers or magnification tools for people who are visually impaired) may not function correctly otherwise.
To help mitigate this issue, we made the setting easy to disable
(Signal Settings → Privacy → Screen security)
, but it’s difficult to accidentally disable. Turning off “Screen security” in Signal Desktop on Windows 11 will always display a warning and require confirmation in order to continue.
This setting is local to your computer and doesn’t apply to screenshots on other devices. If you are communicating with someone who uses a screen reader on macOS or Linux, for example, keeping screen security enabled on your side won’t prevent them from taking screenshots or adversely affect any accessibility software they may be using.
We hope that the AI teams building systems like Recall will think through these implications more carefully in the future. Apps like Signal shouldn’t have to implement “one weird trick” in order to maintain the privacy and integrity of their services without proper developer tools. People who care about privacy shouldn’t be forced to sacrifice accessibility upon the altar of AI aspirations either.
Future Recallections
“Take a screenshot every few seconds” legitimately sounds like a suggestion from a low-parameter LLM that was given a prompt like “How do I add an arbitrary AI feature to my operating system as quickly as possible in order to make investors happy?” — but more sophisticated threats are on the horizon.
The integration of AI agents with pervasive permissions, questionable security hygiene, and an insatiable hunger for data has the potential to break
the blood-brain barrier
between applications and operating systems. This poses a significant threat to Signal, and to every privacy-preserving application in general.
People everywhere rely on Signal to protect their communication, including human rights workers, governments, board rooms, militaries, and millions of individuals around the world for whom privacy is an existential matter. 44053364.article_summary: Signal Desktop引入了一项新的“屏幕安全”设置，旨在防止Windows系统上的电脑截取Signal聊天内容的截图，特别是在微软推出“Recall”功能后。Recall会定期截取用户屏幕并存储为可搜索的数据库。尽管微软在回应批评后对Recall做了调整，但它仍可能威胁隐私保护应用的安全。因此，Signal在Windows 11上默认启用了该保护设置，阻止截图功能，同时提供了可手动关闭的选项，但需要经过警告和确认步骤。Signal此举是为了在缺乏细化开发者工具的情况下保护用户隐私，同时呼吁AI开发团队在未来更慎重考虑隐私与可访问性之间的平衡。
44053364.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Signal的Recall功能及其隐私和安全问题，涉及DRM、数据保护、以及用户对隐私设置的期望。

不同观点：
• **支持Signal的隐私保护措施**：一些用户（如vel0city）认为Signal对Recall功能的保护措施是合理的，尤其是Recall数据库的访问比Signal消息目录更难。同时，vel0city指出，如果攻击者能直接查询Recall数据库，他们很可能已经能够读取设备上的所有Signal消息，因此这种保护是有效的。

• **对元数据保留的担忧**：mmooss指出，虽然Signal有“消失消息”的功能，但该功能不适用于语音和视频通话记录，这些记录会保留在设备上，可能对用户隐私构成威胁，尤其是对人权活动人士等高风险用户。他们认为，Signal应该对所有数据和元数据提供统一的隐私设置，而不是区别对待。

• **对DRM的批评**：一些用户（如Peacefulz、contact9879、WD-42）对Signal需要使用DRM来保护用户数据感到不满，认为这是对用户自由的限制，尤其是当用户需要保护自己免受自己设备上的潜在威胁时。

• **对Windows和操作系统控制的讨论**：plingbang和compsciphd提到，操作系统始终对应用程序有控制权，应用程序只能请求操作系统执行操作。因此，Microsoft有可能修改Recall以捕获DRM标记的内容。此外，compsciphd认为，Signal消息历史以SQLite数据库的形式保存在设备上，本身也是一个隐私问题，因此仅关注Recall的保护可能只是表面功夫。

• **对Signal功能的期望**：kiririn希望Signal能提供将消息包含在iOS备份中的选项，而habitue则表达了对封闭源代码操作系统的普遍不信任，尤其是Microsoft。

补充讨论：
• **Recall功能的实际需求**：bcoates分享了使用Timesnapper（Recall的前身）的经验，认为该功能对于记录工作时间非常有用，并且与多模态LLM结合可能会更加有用。

• **技术实现的争议**：pseudosavant质疑Signal是否在填补一个早就应该解决的漏洞，而josephcsible则关注如何绕过Recall的限制以获取高质量的截图。

• **对Linux的推广**：godelski和enfuse在讨论中提到了Linux作为Windows和MacOS的替代方案，认为Linux的用户体验已经显著提升，并预测其用户群会继续增长。

data.title: 32 bits that changed microprocessor design
data.author: mdp2021
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了贝尔实验室的Bellmac-32微处理器，它是世界上首批32位微处理器之一，对现代智能手机芯片设计产生了深远影响。1982年，Bellmac-32团队在新泽西州莫瑞山的贝尔实验室完成了这一突破性设计。该芯片引入了32位架构，为后续更复杂、更高效的处理器奠定了基础。作者Willie D. Jones指出，Bellmac-32不仅提升了计算能力，还推动了微处理器设计的多项创新，最终促成了今天智能手机中使用的先进芯片技术。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Bellmac-32处理器的技术创新、市场表现及其历史地位

不同观点：
• [zik] 认为 Bellmac-32 的许多特性，如32位架构、两级流水线和按需分页虚拟内存，很大程度上借鉴了早其三年发布的 VAX-11/780 架构。尽管 Bellmac-32 在CMOS技术应用上领先，但文章对其创新性的描述有夸大之嫌。VAX 系列由于未能及时采用LSI技术而逐渐过时。
• [Findecanor] 关注 Bellmac-32 指令集中的 'ASL' 指令，指出其独特的行为，即在左移时保留符号位不变。这种设计在其他ISA中不常见，多数ISA没有单独的算术和逻辑左移指令。
• [macshome] 感叹贝尔实验室对现代技术的深远影响，认为当今社会缺少类似创新环境。
• [didgetmaster] 分享个人经历，提到自己1986年购买的AT&T 6300电脑使用了Intel 8086处理器，间接指出Bellmac-32在市场上的相对弱势。
• [willmarquis] 认为 Bellmac-32 在32位CMOS技术上的领先未能持续，最终被市场淘汰，但其技术影响仍值得肯定，特别是在现代SoC中的遗留影响。
• [rkagerer] 描述了 Bellmac-32 开发过程中因缺乏CAD工具而采用的手工设计方法，强调团队的创新和努力。
• [jandrese] 质疑 Bellmac-32 未成功的原因，特别提到成本问题，并指出8086处理器在市场上的强势表现。

补充讨论：
• Bellmac-32 的技术创新与VAX-11/780 的关系是争议焦点，[zik] 认为前者借鉴了后者，而文章可能夸大了其原创性。
• 不同用户对 Bellmac-32 的市场表现和失败原因有不同看法，[jandrese] 强调成本问题，[willmarquis] 则关注其技术应用的滞后。
• 用户 [joezydeco] 分享了 Bellmac-32 在教育环境中的使用体验，指出其在编程上的趣味性和独特性，如拥有 STRCPY 操作码。

总体而言，讨论围绕 Bellmac-32 的技术创新、市场表现及其在历史上的地位展开，涉及其与VAX-11/780 的关系、市场竞争及技术实现细节。

data.title: The Future of Flatpak
data.author: dxs
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了Flatpak项目的现状与未来。尽管Flatpak在应用打包格式上取得了一定成功，受到开发者和用户欢迎，且被Fedora等Linux发行版采用，但其核心开发进展缓慢。演讲者Sebastian Wick指出，虽然项目维护和安全修复仍在进行，但缺乏对新功能的审查和重大更新。关键开发者的离开导致代码合并过程延迟，新的贡献者也难以快速融入。此外，Wick提到OSTree工具的局限性，并建议采用OCI图像工具以简化开发流程。总体而言，Flatpak功能稳定，但发展受到制约，未来需要更多开发者参与以推动创新。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Flatpak项目的现状、其设计和实用性以及与其他软件打包机制的比较。

不同观点：
• **Flatpak开发停滞**：ndiddy和OsrsNeedsf2P指出，Flatpak项目看似成功，但实际上已经停滞不前，缺乏重大更新。OsrsNeedsf2P特别提到，他曾对Flatpak充满期待，但随着时间的推移，开发活动减少，导致他逐渐失去兴趣。

• **权限问题和兼容性不足**：ndiddy、conradev和amluto提到Flatpak在权限管理上的问题，比如无法为特定功能（如创建虚拟接口）设置权限。amluto还批评了Flatpak在应用程序实例权限管理上的设计缺陷，认为其无法有效隔离不同实例的权限。

• **与其他打包机制的比较**：mrbluecoat和sabslikesobs认为AppImage和传统包管理系统更具优势。mrbluecoat特别提到AppImage的便携性和用户友好性。sabslikesobs则表示，虽然转向Flatpak基础的不变发行版有其优势，但也遇到了许多不稳定和兼容性问题。

• **社区和生态系统支持不足**：bee_rider和sohrob提到Flatpak社区的参与度不高，以及开源社区未能集中资源改进Flatpak。sohrob特别指出，面对众多Linux发行版，社区未能合力推动一个统一的解决方案。

• **设计哲学和整体生态的批评**：zbentley对Flatpak及其他打包工具在Linux生态中的位置进行了深刻批评，认为这些工具虽然在一定程度上解决了应用分发问题，但同时也引入了复杂性和安全问题。ggm则从历史角度分析，认为当前的分裂状态是不可避免的。

补充讨论：
• **具体使用问题**：dbolgheroni分享了在使用Flatpak安装VSCode/Codium时遇到的调试问题，最终转向Snap解决。SubiculumCode也提到在使用Flatpak和Snap时遇到不一致行为和权限错误的问题。

• **对特定发行版的影响**：tomrod关注Flatpak问题对Fedora等发行版的潜在影响，显示出对整体生态健康状况的担忧。

争议焦点：Flatpak是否应由Red Hat等大公司提供更多资源支持以维持其发展，以及是否应集中社区力量推动一个统一的Linux桌面应用分发方案。

The future of Flatpak
By
Joe Brockmeier
May 14, 2025
Linux Application Summit
At the
Linux Application
Summit
(LAS) in April, Sebastian Wick said that, by many metrics,
Flatpak
is doing great. The Flatpak
application-packaging format is popular with upstream developers, and
with many users. More and more applications are being published in the
Flathub
application store, and the
format is even being adopted by Linux distributions like
Fedora. However, he worried that work on the Flatpak project itself
had stagnated, and that there were too few developers able to review
and merge code beyond basic maintenance.
I was not able to attend LAS in person or watch it live-streamed,
so I watched the YouTube
video
of the
talk. The slides are available from the
talk
page
. Wick is a member of the GNOME Project and a Red Hat employee
who works on "
all kinds of desktop plumbing
", including Flatpak
and
desktop
portals
.
Flatpak basics
Flatpak was
originally
developed
by Alexander Larsson, who had been working on similar
projects stretching back to 2007. The
first
release
was as XDG-App in 2015. It was renamed to Flatpak in 2016,
a nod to IKEA's "
flatpacks
"
for delivering furniture.
The Flatpak project provides
command-line
tools
for managing and running Flatpak applications, tools for
building
Flatpak bundles
, and
runtimes
that provide components for Flatpak applications. The project uses
control groups
,
namespaces
,
bind mounts
,
seccomp
, and
Bubblewrap
to provide application isolation ("sandboxing"). Flatpak content is
primarily delivered using
OSTree
,
though support for using
Open
Container Initiative (OCI) images
has been
available
since 2018 and is used by Fedora for its Flatpak applications. The "
Under
the Hood
" page from Flatpak's documentation provides a good
overview of how the pieces fit together.
Slowing development
Wick started his talk by saying that it looks like everything is
great with the Flatpak project, but if one looks deeper, "
you will
notice that it's not being actively developed anymore
". There are
people who maintain the code base and fix security issues, for
example, but "
bigger changes are not really happening
anymore
". He said that there are a bunch of merge requests for new
features, but no one feels responsible for reviewing them, and that is
kind of problematic.

Act now
and you can start with a free trial subscription.
The reason for the lack of reviewers is that key people, such as
Larsson, have left the project. Every now and then, Wick said, Larsson
may get involved if it's necessary, but he is basically not part of
the day-to-day development of the project. Wick said that it is hard
to get new Flatpak contributors involved because it can take months to
get feedback on major changes, and then more months to get another
review. "
This is really not a great way to get someone up to speed,
and it's not a great situation to be in
."
"
Maybe I'm complaining about something that is actually not that
much of an issue
", he said. Flatpak works; it does its job, and
"
we just use it and don't think about it much
". In that sense,
the project is in a good spot. But he has still been thinking
about how the project is "
living with constraints
" because
contributors do not have the opportunity to go in and make bigger
changes.
As an example, Wick said that Red Hat has been doing work that
would allow Flatpaks to be installed as part of a base
installation. The vendor or administrator could specify the
applications to be installed, and a program called
flatpak-preinstall
would take care of the rest. The feature
has been implemented and is planned for inclusion in Red Hat
Enterprise Linux (RHEL) 10. The work was
started
by
Kalev Lember and Owen Taylor last June, but the original pull request
was
closed
by Lember in February as he was leaving Red Hat and would not be
working on it anymore. It was picked up by Wick in February as a
new request
but wasn't reviewed until early May.
OSTree and OCI
Wick's next topic was OCI support in Flatpak. While OSTree has been
a success in some ways, and it is still being maintained, it is not
undergoing active development. He noted that developers have a
"
very narrow set of tools
" for working with OSTree, so building
Flatpaks that use OSTree requires non-standard and bespoke tools, but
there is a whole range of utilities available for working with OCI
images. Even better, tools for working with OCI images "
are all
developed by people other than us, which means we don't actually have
to do the work if we just embrace them
".

主要讨论点：Flatpak项目的现状、其设计和实用性以及与其他软件打包机制的比较。

不同观点：
• **Flatpak开发停滞**：ndiddy和OsrsNeedsf2P指出，Flatpak项目看似成功，但实际上已经停滞不前，缺乏重大更新。OsrsNeedsf2P特别提到，他曾对Flatpak充满期待，但随着时间的推移，开发活动减少，导致他逐渐失去兴趣。

• **权限问题和兼容性不足**：ndiddy、conradev和amluto提到Flatpak在权限管理上的问题，比如无法为特定功能（如创建虚拟接口）设置权限。amluto还批评了Flatpak在应用程序实例权限管理上的设计缺陷，认为其无法有效隔离不同实例的权限。

• **与其他打包机制的比较**：mrbluecoat和sabslikesobs认为AppImage和传统包管理系统更具优势。mrbluecoat特别提到AppImage的便携性和用户友好性。sabslikesobs则表示，虽然转向Flatpak基础的不变发行版有其优势，但也遇到了许多不稳定和兼容性问题。

• **社区和生态系统支持不足**：bee_rider和sohrob提到Flatpak社区的参与度不高，以及开源社区未能集中资源改进Flatpak。sohrob特别指出，面对众多Linux发行版，社区未能合力推动一个统一的解决方案。

• **设计哲学和整体生态的批评**：zbentley对Flatpak及其他打包工具在Linux生态中的位置进行了深刻批评，认为这些工具虽然在一定程度上解决了应用分发问题，但同时也引入了复杂性和安全问题。ggm则从历史角度分析，认为当前的分裂状态是不可避免的。

补充讨论：
• **具体使用问题**：dbolgheroni分享了在使用Flatpak安装VSCode/Codium时遇到的调试问题，最终转向Snap解决。SubiculumCode也提到在使用Flatpak和Snap时遇到不一致行为和权限错误的问题。

• **对特定发行版的影响**：tomrod关注Flatpak问题对Fedora等发行版的潜在影响，显示出对整体生态健康状况的担忧。

争议焦点：Flatpak是否应由Red Hat等大公司提供更多资源支持以维持其发展，以及是否应集中社区力量推动一个统一的Linux桌面应用分发方案。

data.author: isaiahwp
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI在软件开发中的作用及其对开发者工作的影响

不同观点：
• Padolsey认为，对于大多数开发工作，软件开发并没有太多创新，主要是重复使用已有的代码模式。AI编码助手只是强化了这种代码重用，适用于构建常见的CRUD应用，但对于如导弹制导系统等高要求的软件开发，仍需深入学习和理解底层技术。
• Felubra对技术细节和底层硬件有深刻的情感，认为开发者应关注硬件细节，并欣赏与机器交互的美。
• Lunarcave指出，编写代码不仅是最终的产物，还包括在开发过程中所做的权衡。AI可以帮助编写代码，但思考和指导AI生成正确输出仍是人类的工作。
• CGamesPlay认为，过去工程师面临的技术挑战有其历史背景，当前依赖AI可能导致我们不断重复和强化过去30年中积累的技术债务，而非创新。
• Webprofusion将AI与初级开发者类比，认为AI可以完成部分工作，但仍需人工进行修正和优化，最终用户只关心系统功能而非代码质量。

补充讨论：
• Heddycrow以幽默方式表达对文章的共鸣。
• Jboggan担忧未来代码质量下降，因为LLM生成的代码可能冻结过去的错误和不良实践。
• Swyx认为，开发者应具备在不同抽象层次间切换的能力，既能高层次思考，也能深入细节修正代码。
• Malfist批评管理层对AI的不现实期望，认为AI仅在特定情况下有效，且可能导致忽视实际工作需求。
• Jcampuzano2强调，许多非技术人员只关注功能实现，不关心代码质量，这推动了AI在开发中的应用。若放弃对代码美学的追求，AI可能在当前状态下替代许多角色。
• Sgarland担忧AI让那些对技术无热情的人进入行业，类似于DevOps领域中因抽象工具而获得职位的人。
• Airstrike建议，在讨论AI辅助编码时，应明确编程语言、应用领域、使用的AI模型和交互界面，以避免无效讨论。
• Aziell分享了个人经验，指出过度依赖AI助手可能导致停止思考和成长。
• Wewewedxfgdf表达了对编程普及的开放态度。
• Tptacek以电子表格为例，指出对AI取代工作的担忧历史上已有类似讨论。

争议焦点：
• AI在软件开发中的实际作用和其对开发者职业成长的影响。
• 过度依赖AI可能导致代码质量下降与技术债务累积。
• 管理层对AI不切实际的期望和对开发工作的影响。

data.title: Show HN: Defuddle, an HTML-to-Markdown alternative to Readability
data.author: kepano
data.article_summary: Defuddle是一个用于从网页中提取主要内容的工具，能够去除不必要的元素如评论、侧边栏、页眉、页脚等，生成干净、可读的HTML文档。它专为Obsidian Web Clipper设计，适合作为Mozilla Readability的替代品，具有更宽容的元素处理方式，并能一致地处理脚注、代码块等。Defuddle提供三个版本：核心版（无依赖，适合浏览器使用）、完整版（支持数学公式解析）、Node.js版（使用JSDOM，支持Markdown转换）。它提取的内容包括标题、作者、发布日期、主图、网站图标等元数据，并提供调试模式和选择性移除元素的功能。安装通过npm进行，使用时可根据需求配置选项。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于网页内容提取工具的实现、使用场景及相关技术选择的讨论

不同观点：
• [ulrischa] 分享了自己使用PHP构建的类似工具，强调了其易于自托管的特点。
• [tmpfs] 提到不同语言的Readability实现质量参差不齐，推荐了Python的trifatura库，认为其在内容提取和元数据准确性上表现更好，建议与现有实现进行比较以寻求改进。
• [acrophobic] 质疑Mozilla的Readability被遗弃的说法，指出其最新版本发布于两个月前，且维护者活跃地回应问题。
• [Andr2Andr] 提出疑问，询问这种工具的实际使用场景，仅在其他评论中看到用于导出ChatGPT对话为Markdown的例子。
• [jeanlucas] 回应了使用场景的问题，确认Obsidian Web Clipper可用于将ChatGPT对话转换为Markdown或直接打印。
• [revskill] 指出Markdown不支持表单元素，暗示了工具在某些功能上的局限性。
• [billconan] 询问工具是否在后台使用AI模型（如Gemini），以理解使用成本对比Readability。

补充讨论：
• [timdeve] 表示计划尝试将RSS阅读器的可读性功能替换为该工具，并提到由于Pocket即将关闭，可能需要添加“稍后阅读”功能。
• [Tsarp] 对Obsidian Clipper的网站个性化内容提取功能表示赞赏，认为其Markdown提取质量最为可靠。
• [creakingstairs] 提到在研究Obsidian Web Clipper的源码时发现了Defuddle，并计划用于自己的读取和知识库应用。
• [jonplackett] 提问为何某些网站在iPhone的阅读器模式下显示空白页，怀疑是网站故意设置障碍以保护广告收入。
• [rcarmo] 分享了自己多年前实现的Readability算法的经验，最终选择了Python的替代方案，并指出这些工具在定期更新中表现良好。
• [inhumantsar] 提到Readability处于“生命支持”状态，曾参与的Obsidian插件Slurp在维护上遇到困难，尽管如此，Slurp仍不断吸引新用户。

争议焦点：
• Readability的现状及其是否被遗弃。
• 网页内容提取工具在不同网站上的兼容性问题及其背后的技术原因。

总体而言，讨论围绕网页内容提取工具的技术实现、使用场景、兼容性问题及其背后的技术选型展开。

de·​fud·dle /diˈfʌdl/
transitive verb
to remove unnecessary elements from a web page, and make it easily readable.
Beware! Defuddle is very much a work in progress!
Defuddle extracts the main content from web pages. It cleans up web pages by removing clutter like comments, sidebars, headers, footers, and other non-essential elements, leaving only the primary content.
Try the Defuddle Playground →
Features
Defuddle aims to output clean and consistent HTML documents. It was written for
Obsidian Web Clipper
with the goal of creating a more useful input for HTML-to-Markdown converters like
Turndown
.
Defuddle can be used as a replacement for
Mozilla Readability
with a few differences:
More forgiving, removes fewer uncertain elements.
Provides a consistent output for footnotes, math, code blocks, etc.
Uses a page's mobile styles to guess at unnecessary elements.
Extracts more metadata from the page, including schema.org data.
Installation
npm install defuddle
For Node.js usage, you'll also need to install JSDOM:
npm install jsdom

Bundles
Defuddle is available in three different bundles:
Core bundle (
defuddle

Full bundle (

data.title: Airport for DuckDB
data.author: jonbaer
data.article_summary: "Airport"扩展为DuckDB增加了Arrow Flight支持，使其能够通过Arrow Flight服务器查询、修改和存储数据。Arrow Flight是一种基于Apache Arrow的高性能数据服务框架，允许DuckDB访问非表格数据、外部API以及自定义SQL函数，并提供远程执行的用户自定义函数（UDFs）和细粒度的数据访问控制。通过该扩展，DuckDB可以实现原本无法完成的数据服务功能。安装该社区扩展需运行`INSTALL airport FROM community;`和`LOAD airport;`命令。该扩展还支持构建Arrow Flight服务器，并在DuckCon #6会议上进行了介绍。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：DuckDB的功能、优势、局限性以及在实际应用中的使用场景。

不同观点：
• mrbungie：对DuckDB总体持积极评价，认为它是跨平台的强大分析引擎，但对其不支持Iceberg写入感到失望，认为这会增加技术栈的复杂性，需要额外的引擎来处理插入操作。
• r3tr0：非常喜欢DuckDB，并分享了他们在eBPF数据处理中的实际应用，提供了一个沙盒环境来展示其用途。
• k_bx：关注DuckDB是否支持加载IPC文件，因为这是他们在将数据转换为Parquet文件之前进行追加操作的重要需求。
• vkaku：赞赏DuckDB及其相关工具（如fuzzycomplete和lindel）的功能，表现出对DuckDB生态系统的喜爱。
• rubenvanwyk：关心数据源和目标是否都需要设置Flight服务器，并质疑这种方法在与第三方服务集成时的实用性。
• blef：认为DuckDB及其相关功能是一个有趣的思想实验，可以实现所有数据处理任务都通过SQL完成，将其比作MCPs（主控程序）在DuckDB世界中的表现。

补充讨论：
• the_optimist：质疑这种方法的实际应用场景，认为需要明确解释在什么情况下这种方案是最佳解决方案，尤其是在替代远程DuckDB实例和DB服务器的情况下。
• 对Iceberg写入支持的缺乏（mrbungie提出）和IPC文件加载问题（k_bx提出）是两个主要的技术限制，可能影响用户的技术选型。
• 对DuckDB实际应用的讨论，如r3tr0提供的系统级指标处理案例，展示了其在特定领域的成功应用。

争议焦点：DuckDB在处理复杂数据操作（如Iceberg写入和IPC文件处理）时的能力不足，以及其在实际应用场景中的适用性问题（the_optimist的观点）。

44028616.article_content:
The
Airport
extension brings
Arrow Flight
support to
DuckDB
, enabling DuckDB to query, modify, and store data via Arrow Flight servers. A DuckDB extension is a plugin that expands DuckDBâs core functionality by adding new capabilities.
To understand the rationale behind the development of this extension, check out the
motivation for creating the extension
.
Getting started
The Airport extension is a
DuckDB community extension
. To install it, run the following SQL inside DuckDB:
INSTALL airport
FROM
community;
To load the extension you can then execute:
LOAD airport;
If you wish to build the extension from source see these
instructions
.
What can I do with the Airport extension that I canât do with DuckDB now?
With the Airport extension you can:
Query data that DuckDB canât normally accessâeither because itâs non-tabular or in an unsupported format. Even external APIs. It all depends what the server allows.
Add custom
scalar
or
table returning
SQL functions not available in DuckDB.
Provide User Defined Functions (UDFs) for DuckDB that execute remotely.
Serve data with fine-grained access control, filtering both rows and columns based on user permissions.
Access and provide
Data-as-a-Service
.
What is Arrow Flight?
From the Apache Arrow Documentation:
Arrow Flight
is an RPC framework for high-performance data services based on
Apache Arrow
and is built on top of
gRPC
and the
Arrow IPC format
.
Flight is organized around streams of Arrow record batches
1
, being either downloaded from or uploaded to another service. A set of metadata methods offers discovery and introspection of streams, as well as the ability to implement application-specific methods.
Methods and message wire formats are defined by
Protobuf
, enabling interoperability with clients that may support gRPC and Arrow separately, but not Flight. However, Flight implementations include further optimizations to avoid overhead in usage of Protobuf (mostly around avoiding excessive memory copies).
What is an Apache Arrow âFlightâ?
An Apache Arrow flight (hereafter referred to simply as a âflightâ) is a source or destination for data that is accessible via the Apache Arrow Flight RPC framework. Each flight has a schema and one or more endpoints, that may offer one or more locations.
You can think of flights to be simliar to be a collection of files that share the same schema or even more apt a database table that is stored on a remote server. Apache Arrow Flight servers often provide many different flights.
How does Airport work with DuckDB?
Airport is an extension written in C++ for DuckDB version 1.3.0 or later, it utilizes the Apache Arrow library.
How can I build an Arrow Flight Server?
Start by reading the
basics of implementing an Arrow Flight Server
.
Conference Presentations
Rusty Conover presented the Airport extension in a presentation titled
âAirport For DuckDB: Letting DuckDB take flight.â
at DuckCon #6.
Footnotes
A record batch is a collection of equal-length arrays that all match a schema.

data.title: “Secret Mall Apartment,” a Protest for Place
data.author: rufus_foreman
data.article_summary: 《Secret Mall Apartment》讲述了2003年美国罗得岛的一群艺术家秘密栖居于一家繁忙购物中心，并在未经许可的情况下生活了约四年。他们在商场中一个无人注意的隐蔽空间里安家，利用旧货店的物品布置居所，以此抗议这座毫无生气的消费主义神殿。这群艺术家此前曾将废弃工厂改造成住家和艺术场所，但被开发项目驱逐。新建造的商场进一步分隔了城市中的贫富区域，激起了他们的反抗情绪。他们偶尔使用商场的公共设施，并通过建造墙壁隐藏住所，成功多年未被发现。这部纪录片通过他们的视角，揭示了对城市过度开发和现代消费文化的无声抗议。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：一群人在未经授权的情况下占用空间并拍摄纪录片，引发了不同角度的讨论和评价。

不同观点：
• [Animats] 认为该事件在2003年发生，并于2018年被报道，带有图片和视频，但本质上是为电影做的公关宣传。
• [neom] 对该项目持负面态度，提到项目中有人曾为他工作，但背后搞小动作，最终导致他被解雇并失去对创业公司的控制，认为该项目不诚实。
• [toofy] 对该项目持积极态度，提到在影院观看了相关纪录片，认为影片非常吸引人，特别是偷运家具和建材的片段，让人感到紧张刺激。
• [Stevvo] 认为此类事件在美国被当作故事和电影来讲述很奇怪，因为在欧洲，人们会随意占用任何合适的建筑，这种行为并不稀奇。
• [palmfacehn] 提供了一个类似的案例，提到有人曾在汉普斯特德荒原下建地堡居住两年，暗示这种占用空间的行为并非孤例。
• [gravitronic] 对项目的“抗议”标签持怀疑态度，认为事后添加的社会行动标签不诚实，认为做酷的事情不需要特别理由，不需要赋予额外意义。
• [deadbabe] 对秘密居住空间感兴趣，询问其他人是否有类似居住经历。
• [sandspar] 观察到项目领导者年龄较大，提到这种年长领导者吸引年轻追随者的模式在历史上多次出现，如诗人金斯堡和涂鸦团队等。
• [GuinansEyebrows] 对该事件持积极态度，认为这是他最喜欢的美国当代占屋案例之一。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是该项目的真实动机和事后赋予的社会行动标签是否诚实。
• 不同文化和地区对占用空间行为的接受度和看法不同，欧洲和美国的比较体现了这种差异。
• 对项目领导者的年龄和影响力进行了社会学和历史学的分析，提到这种年长领导者吸引年轻追随者的模式。
• 对纪录片的观感评价不一，有的认为紧张刺激，有的认为附加的抗议标签不必要。

44067767.article_content:
In 2003, a group of Rhode Island artists created a secret living space within a busy shopping mall and lived there off and on, undetected, for about four years.
Why?
The new documentary
Secret Mall Apartment
, now in select theaters nationwide, tells the story of eight Providence-based artists who, although they periodically hint at their left-leaning politics, admirably dedicate their time and skills to projects paying tribute to the first-responder firemen who perished on 9/11, the victims of the 1995 Oklahoma City bombing, and sick children in hospitals. It’s touching. You root for them.
Oh, and they live in their local mall.
Directed by Jeremy Workman and produced by actor Jesse Eisenberg, the documentary features grainy 2000s cell-phone camera footage of the cast of characters—all artists but also intimate friends—as well as modern-day interviews about their time living in the mall.
The ringleader is Michael Townsend, who is fifty-four now and hatched the mall apartment project in his early thirties. When the Providence Place Mall was under construction, one of Townsend’s friends noticed that there was an odd space that didn’t seem to have a dedicated purpose. Townsend took the lead on furnishing the space with goods from the Salvation Army and other thrift stores.
Townsend
said
in an interview, “It was windowless, lifeless concrete, very industrial, not designed to be comfortable in any way—that said, myself and my comrades are all repeat offenders of moving into mill spaces that are big and industrial and making them into our homes—that’s our whole bag.”
The original plan was to stay a week.
The latest essay every day.
Email
*
Sign Up
“It trains you to be in a mindset that you have a sort of role as steward of spaces that you will temporarily make something different and uniquely beautiful, and just as easily remove it,” he added.
The artists’ squatting was a statement. They hated the mall. By “living” there, without permission or anyone even noticing (the logistics of their apartment living are some of the most interesting parts of the movie) the artists attempt to domesticate and humanize this soulless shrine to consumerism foisted on them by city planners.
These Gen X and Millennial artists had only known late twentieth- and early twenty-first-century post-industrial Providence, and they made home out of the little they had to work with. They had repurposed abandoned textile mill buildings into apartments, art galleries, and warehouse party spots in an area known as Fort Thunder. Developers eventually demolished Fort Thunder, kicking the artists out. Not long after, developers began construction on the Providence Place Mall, which, seemingly by design, separated the working class areas of Providence from the wealthier areas. For many locals, it was a lot of development all at once, the mall in particular being a radical transformation for their city.
Deciding to squat in the mall they hated was a unique form of defiance against lifeless urban sprawl, but the sentiment was not exactly new. From the Southern Agrarians of the 1930s to Richard Weaver and beyond, there is a long history of conservative resistance to modernity, particularly the industrial revolution.
Watching the film, my mind first went to Russell Kirk and Wendell Berry and their
low opinion
of bulldozers, but even more so to the great localist conservative Bill Kauffman. Of his own often-mentioned and beloved hometown of Batavia, New York, Kauffman
wrote
in 2017, “Our city fathers rushed headlong into this mad program whereby the federal government paid Batavia to knock down its past: the mansions of the founders, sandstone churches, the brick shops of Main Street—the whole damned—or, rather, blessed—thing.”
“Batavia,” he continued, “tore out its five-block heart and filled the cavity with a ghastly mall, a colossal failure built in the aptly named Brutalist style. We are used today in urban-planning texts as a case study in disaster.”
Lamenting the mall and the demolition of old Batavia, Kauffman added, “In some ways we were a typical small American city but in other ways we were ‘Batavia’—our own place. We did not yet bow down before the new American royalty: Burger King and Dairy Queen.”
The tenants of
Secret Mall Apartment
frequented the mall food court of Burger Kings, Dairy Queens, or whatever interchangeable fast-food offerings were available. They used the public bathrooms. They built a cinder block wall to further conceal their hiding place, with each occupant having a key to the door, where they could enter at any time to play video games or spend the night.
It was meant as an unusual form of protest, only known to them. The same generic mall imposed on Providence, impervious to the organic customs and character of the place, was also detached enough from the human beings who lived there that the building’s authorities didn’t detect a gaggle of them inhabiting the property for four years.
How they are eventually discovered i

data.title: Richard Garwin’s role in designing the hydrogen bomb was obscured
data.author: LAsteNERD
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对Richard Garwin和Theodore Hall的历史背景及其在核武器发展中的角色进行分析和讨论。

不同观点：
• **Hilift**的观点：强调Theodore Hall和Richard Garwin在同一时间都在芝加哥大学，且都是神童。Hilift详细介绍了Hall的间谍活动及其对苏联提供原子弹细节的文件，以及他在麦卡锡时代的调查中被保护的背景。Hilift认为Hall虽然涉及间谍活动，但仍被空军重用并完成了导弹项目开发。

• **jasonhong**的观点：提到Garwin在IBM的贡献，包括磁共振成像、触屏显示器、激光打印机等。jasonhong特别强调了Garwin在23岁时设计了第一个可用的氢弹，突显了他在核武器发展中的重要角色。

• **smartbit**的观点：指出Garwin是Pugwash会议的成员，积极参与多个国际科学会议，并与苏联科学家合作，提出限制核武库和太空武器的建议。smartbit强调了Garwin在国际科学合作和军备控制方面的贡献。

• **Supermancho**的观点：质疑冷战期间关于核武器威力的评估，特别是对一个相当于600,000个广岛原子弹威力的核武器的实际效果提出疑问。Supermancho探讨了评估中的潜在误差来源，如空气压力和爆炸效果的差异。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：Hilift和jasonhong对Hall和Garwin在核武器发展中的角色持不同看法。Hilift更关注Hall的间谍活动及其政治背景，而jasonhong则强调Garwin在核武器设计和科技领域的成就。
• **合作与冲突**：smartbit补充了Garwin在军备控制和国际合作方面的努力，与Hilift和jasonhong对Garwin在核武器发展中角色的强调形成对比。
• **技术评估**：Supermancho对核武器威力的技术评估提出质疑，提供了一个关于核武器实际效果的不同视角。

总体来看，讨论围绕Garwin和Hall的个人历史、技术成就及政治影响展开，涉及他们在核武器发展和军备控制中的不同角色和贡献。

• **smartbit**的观点：指出Garwin是Pugwash会议的成员，积极参与多个国际科学会议，并与苏联科学家合作，提出限制核武库和太空武器的建议。smartbit强调了Garwin在国际科学合作和军备控制方面的贡献。

• **Supermancho**的观点：质疑冷战期间关于核武器威力的评估，特别是对一个相当于600,000个广岛原子弹威力的核武器的实际效果提出疑问。Supermancho探讨了评估中的潜在误差来源，如空气压力和爆炸效果的差异。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：Hilift和jasonhong对Hall和Garwin在核武器发展中的角色持不同看法。Hilift更关注Hall的间谍活动及其政治背景，而jasonhong则强调Garwin在核武器设计和科技领域的成就。
• **合作与冲突**：smartbit补充了Garwin在军备控制和国际合作方面的努力，与Hilift和jasonhong对Garwin在核武器发展中角色的强调形成对比。
• **技术评估**：Supermancho对核武器威力的技术评估提出质疑，提供了一个关于核武器实际效果的不同视角。

总体来看，讨论围绕Garwin和Hall的个人历史、技术成就及政治影响展开，涉及他们在核武器发展和军备控制中的不同角色和贡献。

主要讨论点：对AI领域中“护城河”（moat）的讨论，包括哪些因素能够构成持久的竞争优势。

不同观点：
• [smodo] 认为许多关于AI未来的文章过于自信且预测性强，将其比作冒险小说，暗示这些文章可能夸大了对未来的预见能力。

• [AnotherGoodName] 指出，虽然AI公司可能拥有难以复制的训练模型权重作为护城河，但若在基础设施上投入5亿美元，则类似于航空公司的高债务低利润模式，质疑这种高投入是否能形成有效的护城河。

• [djoldman] 认为模型、基础设施和应用都可能成为护城河，目前尚无定论。不同类型的护城河可能在不同层面上发挥作用。

• [gwern] 关注文章的写作风格，指出作者让ChatGPT代写文章的现象，并对其合理性提出质疑。

• [KasianFranks] 强调独特、专业、高价值且难以复制的数据和数据集将成为新的竞争优势和护城河。

• [mhb] 认为AI领域的竞争是赢家通吃，护城河的概念可能不适用。高投资是否合理取决于赢得整个市场的可能性。

• [alephnerd] 强烈反对关于AI和ML的炒作，认为这种炒作可能导致行业泡沫和崩溃，类似于2000年代的电信泡沫。还指出，开发基础模型和数据中心的成本不能构成有效的护城河。

• [VirusNewbie] 不同意“模型不能构成护城河”的观点，以Meta和Microsoft为例，指出他们尚未推出最先进的基础模型，说明模型仍可能是重要的竞争优势。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于哪些因素可以构成AI领域的有效护城河，包括模型、基础设施、应用和数据等不同方面。
• 投资与回报的关系也是一个讨论重点，特别是高额投资是否能够带来可持续的竞争优势。
• 对AI和ML领域过度炒作的担忧以及可能引发的行业问题也被提及。

KAN是一种不同于传统多层感知器（MLP）的表示方法，通过重构MLP中的权重矩阵-向量乘法来参数化激活函数。尽管KAN的理论证明不如MLP完善，但它在可解释性和数据效率方面提供了新的探索方向。KAN基于Kolmogorov-Arnold表示定理，能表示连续光滑的多变量函数，通过优化损失函数来学习这些函数的参数。文章还讨论了KAN层的定义及其参数化方法。

44066696.article_content:
The Annotated Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (KAN)
An annotated guide to the Kolmogorov-Arnold Network
if the LaTeX is not loading, refresh the page.
This post is analogous to and heavily inspired by the
Annotated Transformer
but for KANs. It is fully functional as a standalone notebook, and provides intuition along with the code. Most of the code was written to be easy to follow and to mimic the structure of a standard deep learning model in PyTorch, but some parts like training loops and visualization code were adapted from the
original codebase
. We decided to remove some sections from the original paper that were deemed unimportant, and also includes some extra works to motivate future research on these models.
The original paper is titled
“KAN: Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks”
, and the authors on this paper are:
Ziming Liu, Yixuan Wang, Sachin Vaidya, Fabian Ruehle, James Halverson, Marin Soljačić, Thomas Y. Hou, and Max Tegmark.
Introduction
Deep neural networks have been the driving force of developments in AI in the last decade. However, they currently suffer from several known issues such as a lack of interpretability, scaling issues, and data inefficiency – in other words, while they are powerful, they are not a perfect solution.
Teaser figure taken from the original
KAN paper.
Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) are an alternative representation to standard multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs). In short, they parameterize activation functions by re-wiring the “multiplication” in an MLP’s weight matrix-vector multiplication into function application. While KANs are not nearly as provably accomplished as MLPs, they are an exciting prospect for the field of AI and deserve some time for exploration.
I have separated this article into two sections. Parts I & II describe a minimal KAN architecture and training loop without an emphasis on B-spline optimizations. You can use
the minimal KAN notebook
if you’re interested in KANs at a high-level. Parts III & IV describe B-spline specific optimizations and an application of KANs, which includes a bit of extra machinery in the KAN code. You can use the
full KAN notebook
if you want to follow along there.
Background and Motivation
Before jumping into the implementation details, it is important to take a step back and understand why one should even care about these models. It is quite well known that Multi-layer Perceptrons (MLPs) have the “Universal Approximation Theorem”
, which provides a theoretical guarantee for the
existence
of an MLP that can approximate any function
This is a very strong guarantee that usually isn't actually true. Generally, we have some provable guarantee for a class of functions that we actually care about approximating, like say the set of functions in L1 or the set of smooth, continuous functions.
up to some error \(\epsilon\). While this guarantee is important, in practice, it says nothing about how difficult it is to find such an MLP through, say, optimization with stochastic gradient descent.
KANs admit a similar guarantee through the Kolmogorov-Arnold representation theorem, though with a caveat
See section [Are Stacked KAN Layers a Universal Approximator?]
. Formally, the theorem states that for a set of covariates \((x_1,x_2,...,x_n)\), we can write any
continuous, smooth
Smooth in this context means in $C^{\infty}$, or infinitely differentiable.
function \(f(x_1,...,x_n) : \mathcal{D} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}\) over a bounded domain \(\mathcal{D}\)
Because it is bounded, the authors argue that we can normalize the input to the space $[0,1]^{n}$, which is what is assumed in the original paper.
in the form
$$
f(x_1,...,x_n) = \sum_{q=0}^{2n} \Phi_{q} \left( \sum_{p=1}^{n} \Phi_{q,p} (x_p) \right)
$$
where \(\Phi_{q,p}, \Phi_{q}\) are univariate functions from \(\mathbb{R}\) to \(\mathbb{R}\). In theory, we can parameterize and learn these (potentially non-smooth and highly irregular) univariate functions \(\Phi_{q,p}, \Phi_{q}\) by optimizing a loss function similar to any other deep learning model. But it’s not that obvious how one would “parameterize” a function the same way you would parameterize a weight matrix. For now, just assume that it is possible to parameterize these functions – the original authors choose to use a B-spline, but there is little reason to be stuck on this choice.
What is a KAN?
The expression from the theorem above does not describe a KAN with $L$ layers. This was an initial point of confusion for me. The universal approximation guarantee is only for models specifically in the form of the Kolmogorov-Arnold representation, but currently we have no notion of a “layer” or anything scalable. In fact, the number of parameters in the above theorem is a function of the number of covariates and not the choice of the engineer! Instead, the authors define a KAN layer \(\mathcal{K}_{m,n}\) with input dimension \(n\) and output dimension \(m\) as a parameterized matrix of univariate functions, \(\Phi = \{\Phi_{i,j}\}_{i \in [m], j

44068204.article_content:
title
Sketchy Calendar
dated
Q2 2025
author
Marcel Goethals, Paul Sonnentag
related
Sketchy Feel
Sketchy calendar
When it comes to calendars, you can choose between using a digital calendar app or getting a paper calendar. They both allow you to keep track of things like doctor appointments, work meetings or birthdays, so you can keep a clear head and be sure that you won’t forget anything. But while the two approaches may seem similar on the surface, they’re radically different in the kinds of trade-offs they make.
In this project, we’re exploring what it would mean to have a calendar that combines the convenience of a digital calendar with the simplicity and expressivity you get from pen & paper.
Calendar apps
On the one hand, calendar apps like Google Calendar offer many convenient features. You can easily switch between different (daily, weekly and monthly) views. All your events are synced across your devices. You can send calendar invites and even create shared calendars with other people, so when you plan something that affects others, you can check their availability.
While powerful, Google Calendar’s design imposes a strict view of what a calendar event is. If you have tentative plans like “lunch with a friend sometime next week” there is no obvious way to add this to your calendar in a way that differentiates it from an important appointment that can’t be missed.
Calendar apps can also feel very sterile and impersonal. All events are visually uniform, regardless of importance, even across different contexts. Events on my company calendar (which I only need to see for coordination) exist alongside my personal commitments with no visual hierarchy.
A calendar app
could
be a deeply personal place for collecting memories, which allows users to reflect on how they are spending their time. In practice, calendar apps are primarily a tool for scheduling meetings.
Paper calendars
In contrast, using pen & paper is much more flexible. You can get calendars that offer varying degrees of structure, from completely blank notebooks with no imposed format to more structured planners that have preprinted pages for months, weeks, and days with dedicated sections for things like tasks and timelines. The preprinted structure acts more like a guideline than a requirement. It is easy to ignore: Users can draw arrows, doodle, and mark rough timeframes for activities, without being forced to fit a predetermined schema.
This versatility extends way beyond scheduling events—the same pages can accommodate things like meeting notes, meal plans, to-dos, and habit tracking.
Unlike apps that can only capture events, paper calendars grow naturally into personal spaces, capable of capturing the various aspects of daily life, like meal plans, to-do lists or habit trackers.
Can we combine both worlds?
What if you could have a digital calendar that combined the strengths of both the paper and the digital world?
Some calendar apps have attempted to address this question by
adding more features
.
Hey Calendar
, for example, allows users to personalize their calendar by assigning titles or background images to days. Beyond events, users can also add unscheduled to-dos and track daily habits.
While certainly an improvement over regular calendar apps, they remain constrained to the limits of the ‘app’ paradigm: users cannot customize their experience in ways the developers didn’t anticipate, they’re stuck with workarounds or feature requests that — if implemented — will inevitably lead to feature creep, which will add complexity for all users.
Instead, we’re interested in taking the paper calendar as a starting point. Pen & paper, straight out of the box, affords a level of customization and personalization that we rarely see in the world of software. But its unstructured nature also makes it difficult to add any of the convenient functionalities that we get when we digitize information. This project explores this trade-off. How far can we get by taking a simple digital notebook (iPad & pencil) and adding a small amount of structure?
These are some of the questions we intend to explore:
Is it possible to create interconnected daily, weekly and monthly views like a traditional calendar app?
How might sketched annotations meaningfully interact with formal calendar events?
How would shared calendars or calendar invites work in such a semi-structured system?
How can users personalize their calendars by adding custom dynamic behavior? For example, how might I add a habit tracker or a time tracker, all while preserving the sketchy, personal quality?
Here is a little sneak preview of what a sketchy calendar could look like. We will soon
share more about how this works and what we’ve learned building it.

44068204.article_summary: 《Sketchy Calendar》探讨了结合数字日历便利性和纸笔日历表达力与灵活性的可能性。文章比较了数字日历（如Google Calendar）和纸质日历的优缺点。数字日历功能强大，便于同步和共享，但过于刻板，难以体现事件的灵活性，且视觉上缺乏层次。纸质日历则灵活多变，允许用户随意标注、涂画，能兼顾多种日常需求，如笔记和习惯跟踪。文章提出，是否能创造一种结合两者优势的日历，既具备数字化的便利，又保留纸质的个性化和灵活性。项目将探讨如何在数字化笔记本上添加适度结构，实现如互连视图、手绘注释与正式事件互动、共享日历等功能，同时保持个性化特色。

data.author: sailE
data.article_summary: 文章总结了Stripe在2025年Stripe Sessions大会上披露的工程成就。2024年，Stripe平均每天完成1,145个代码合并请求并部署到生产环境，同时全年API不稳定时间不到一分钟。Stripe拥有约8,500名员工，其中40%从事工程工作，这意味着每位工程师平均每三天就将一个变更部署到生产环境。这一成就展示了Stripe卓越的工程文化和高效的自动化测试、部署及回滚机制。根据DORA 2024报告，Stripe的部署频率和稳定性使其跻身顶级软件交付表现的前1%。文章强调了Stripe在高强度和大规模下保持高速交付的能力，并指出其成功源于先进的工程文化、强大的工具支持和工程师的自主性。最终，目标不是追求高频部署，而是消除阻碍快速交付的障碍。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Stripe的高频代码部署和工程绩效衡量标准的有效性

不同观点：
• **支持高频部署的观点**：
   - **darth_avocado**：认为Stripe能够频繁且持续地将代码推送到生产环境是非常 impressive 的，尤其是在金融行业，错误容忍度极低，因此Stripe的做法非常值得赞赏。
   - **danpalmer**：高频小变更的部署方式是可行的，并且在工程组织中是可实现的。小变更意味着更容易的代码审查、更低的部署风险，同时还能推动更好的工具和变更管理。
   - **sverhagen**：一旦团队适应了这种高频部署模式，它实际上比每月做一次大版本发布更容易，因为每次发布的变更量和风险都会更小。

• **质疑高频部署和PR数量作为绩效指标的观点**：
   - **TowerTall**：质疑为何Stripe需要如此频繁地更改软件，这种高频变更的必要性受到怀疑。
   - **cuttothechase**：认为PR数量并不能有效衡量工程绩效或产品表现，甚至可能只是一种可以被操纵的虚荣指标。
   - **xeromal**：PR合并数量完全不能作为有用的衡量标准。
   - **dgrin91**：认为PR数量并不能展示Stripe是否在提供实际的价值，而只是显示他们在“交付某些东西”。

• **关于工程团队分工和核心业务的讨论**：
   - **nitwit005**：质疑Stripe的团队中有多少人真正从事核心支付流程的开发，而不是从事次要的功能或工具。

• **工程效率与技术架构的讨论**：
   - **metalrain**：高频部署的工程模式对Stripe这样的公司有意义，因为他们无法承受停机损失。但对于小型公司，选择更多的停机时间可能更合理，从而减少工程投入。
   - **madduci**：询问是否存在关于Stripe的技术架构和基础设施的公开资料。

补充讨论：
• **对Stripe技术文章链接失效的讨论**：
   - **arp242**：提到一个关于Stripe架构的文章链接失效，并提供了网页存档链接。

• **关于非技术人员对工程实践影响的讨论**：
   - **revskill**：暗示非技术人员有时会阻碍工程实践的现实落地。

• **关于Stripe复杂性的讨论**：
   - **Sytten**：认为Stripe的成功源于其简单性，但如今这种简单性已不复存在，最近集成Stripe的开发者可能会感受到这种复杂性。

争议焦点：
• 争议的核心在于高频部署和PR数量是否能作为衡量工程绩效的有效指标。一部分人认为这是一种值得追求的做法，而另一部分人则认为这是虚荣指标，无法展示实际的价值。

44065680.article_content:
Slide from opening keynote of Stripe Sessions 2025
There is a
recent video
of Patrick Collison at Stripe Sessions 2025 stating that in 2024 Stripe did on average
1,145 pull requests per day
. Not just creating them, but actually finishing them; "
fully shipped into production
". All whilst having less than a minute of API unreliability for the entire year.
Stripe has roughly 8,500 employees (
BI, 2025
). 40% or so in engineering (
Forbes, 2022
). With some napkin math assuming a similar distribution today, that would mean on average each engineer ships at least 1 change to production every 3 days. That is pretty incredible for the scale at which Stripe operates ($1.4 trillion(!) payment volume
in 2024
).
Though Stripe is well-known for their strong engineering culture, a number like that really puts things into perspective. According to
DORA 2024
(research by Google on software delivery & operations) elite software delivery performance does "multiple deploys per day" with a 5% failure rate. It's probably not a stretch to say Stripe is in the top 1% of elite performers by these measurements alone.
One thousand one hundred forty-five deployments to production. Per day.
To achieve that kind of delivery performance with that many people is honestly amazing. On its own, the "1 change to production every 3 days" per engineer might get mixed reactions. "We did 5 production deploys in one day at company XYZ!". But did they do it consistently for an entire year? With less than a minute of downtime?
It's not impossible but just thinking about the throughput really says something about how the ship is being run. Shipping safely at this velocity and scale implies heavy investment in automated tests, deployments, rollbacks, observability, code ownership and so forth. All those things pop-up in your favorite flavor of devops survey but you rarely see it operationalized at this level.
There are quite a few nuggets scattered on the internet regarding how Stripe does things (ex.
#1
,
#2
,
#3
) and in general the conclusion is that they have a very demanding but very advanced engineering culture.
[...] what I learned at Stripe was nothing like I had experienced in more than 20 years in the industry.
What I Learned At Stripe (Steinkamp, 2022)
Few companies operate at Stripe's scale, intensity and mission-critical level. But that shouldn't be a deterrence for aspiring to this kind of clarity, confidence, and velocity in engineering. It's a reflection of engineering culture done right; trusting changes, the tooling necessary to do that, autonomy of engineers and a relentless focus on continuously shipping value for users.
The goal is not 1,145 deployments per day. It's removing the friction that makes that pace impossible. What's really stopping you from rapidly shipping value to users?

44068243.article_content:
The NCL Salter ship just metres from Johan Helberg's house in Byneset, near Trondheim.
Photograph: Joanne Fielder
View image in fullscreen
The NCL Salter ship just metres from Johan Helberg's house in Byneset, near Trondheim.
Photograph: Joanne Fielder
Norway
‘It was so unreal’: Norwegian man wakes to cargo ship in his garden
A 135-metre container vessel ran aground in Byneset, near Trondheim, narrowly missing a house
Miranda Bryant
Nordic correspondent
Thu 22 May 2025 12.56 EDT
First published on Thu 22 May 2025 12.06 EDT
Share
A Norwegian man has spoken of the “unreal” moment he woke up to discover that a 135-metre container ship had crashed into his front garden.
The cargo vessel, the NCL Salten, had run aground just before 5am on Thursday after entering the Trondheim fjord on its way to the western town of Orkanger.
An astonished neighbour watched as the ship, which was travelling at about 16 knots (approximately 30km/h), headed straight for the shore into Johan Helberg’s garden, narrowly missing his house.
Helberg
,
who lives in Byneset, near Trondheim, awoke to his neighbour ringing his doorbell. He looked out of his window to see the ship’s bow.
“I went to the window and was quite astonished to see a big ship,” Helberg told the Guardian. “I had to bend my neck to see the top of it. It was so unreal.”
View image in fullscreen
Johan Helberg in front of the boat.
Photograph: Joanne Fielder
There were 16 crew members, among them Norwegians, Lithuanians, Ukrainians and Russians, on board the Cyprus-registered ship. There were no reports of injuries or oil spills. Police are investigating the incident and have identified one suspect on board the boat.
“Normally ships turn left or right into the fjord. But this went straight ahead,” Helberg, who has lived in the house for 25 years, added. “It was very close to the house.”
View image in fullscreen
Photograph: Jan Langhaug/EPA
Per Christian Stokke, a spokesperson for Trøndelag police district, told NRK: “There is one person on board the boat who has been identified as a suspect.”
Police have interviewed the crew and are working on several theories, including technical failure and human error.
The shipping company, North Sea Container Line (NCL), said the shipmate had been named a suspect but that it was a routine police procedure.
NCL’s chief executive, Bente Hetland, said there was “no reason to believe this was intentional”.
“Incidents like this should not happen, and we have started an investigation into the causes. Today, we are relieved that there were no injuries, and our main focus is on the people near the ship and our crew,” she added.
View image in fullscreen
Photograph: Jan Langhaug/EPA
The ship remained stuck aground on Thursday after the first attempt to remove it was unsuccessful. They planned to try again in the evening during high tide.

data.title: In 3.5 years, Notepad.exe goes from "barely maintained" to "it writes for you"
data.author: CharlesW
data.article_summary: 截至2021年底，Windows内置的记事本文本编辑器鲜少有重大更新，因此一次轻微的重新设计和几个新设置就被视为重大更新。此后，更新变得更加频繁，但大多集中在生成式人工智能功能上。2023年11月，微软测试了允许用户使用AI重写或总结文本的功能。最新更新进一步扩展，允许用户根据基本指令从零开始生成AI文本（称为"Write"功能）。这些AI功能需要微软账户，并消耗每月分配的AI信用额度。免费用户每月15个信用，付费订阅用户则有60个。此外，微软还为Paint和Snipping Tool发布了预览更新，加入更多AI相关功能，如Paint的贴纸生成器和智能选择工具，以及Snipping Tool的颜色选择器和自动裁剪功能。这些更新目前正在Windows Insider的Canary和Dev渠道中推出。

By late 2021, major updates for Windows' built-in Notepad text editor had been so rare for so long that a gentle redesign and a handful of new settings were
rated as a major update
. New updates have become much more common since then, but like the rest of Windows, recent additions have been overwhelmingly weighted in the direction of generative AI.
In November, Microsoft
began testing an update
that allowed users to rewrite or summarize text in Notepad using generative AI. Another preview update today
takes it one step further
, allowing you to write AI-generated text from scratch with basic instructions (the feature is called Write, to differentiate it from the earlier Rewrite).
Like Rewrite and Summarize, Write requires users to be signed into a Microsoft Account, because using it requires you to use your monthly allotment of Microsoft's AI credits.
Per this support page
, users without a paid Microsoft 365 subscription get 15 credits per month. Subscribers with Personal and Family subscriptions get 60 credits per month instead.
Microsoft notes that all AI features in Notepad can be disabled in the app's settings, and obviously, they won't be available if you use a local account instead of a Microsoft Account.
Microsoft is also releasing preview updates for Paint and Snipping Tool, two other bedrock Windows apps that hadn't seen much by way of major updates before the Windows 11 era. Paint's features are also mostly AI-related, including a "sticker generator" and an AI-powered smart select tool "to help you isolate and edit individual elements in your image." A new "welcome experience" screen that appears the first time you launch the app will walk you through the (again, mostly AI-related) new features Microsoft has added to Paint in the last couple of years.
Snipping Tool gets two new features. One is a color picker that will let you see the hex, RGB, or HSL values of colors in a given screenshot. The other is a "perfect screenshot" option that will attempt to automatically crop app windows or other elements onscreen without requiring you to edit it manually after you capture it.
The perfect screenshot feature appears to use local processing rather than cloud processing, because it requires a
Copilot+ PC
. This means using it doesn't require AI credits, but it will also only function on brand-new PCs with certain Qualcomm Snapdragon, Intel Core Ultra, or AMD Ryzen AI processors inside.
These updates are rolling out to Windows Insiders in the Canary and Dev channels, which get new features faster than the Beta or Release Preview channels but are also less stable. Not all of these features will make it to the general public, but the ones that do should be released in the next few weeks or months.

data.title: Show HN: ClipJS – Edit your videos from a PC or phone
data.author: mohyware
data.article_summary: Clip JS 是一款免费、开源的在线视频编辑工具，无需下载、注册或担心水印。用户可以通过电脑或手机访问，直接使用而无需观看广告或注册账户。它支持修剪视频、去除不必要部分，以及将多个视频、图片、文本和音频合并为一体。所有操作在浏览器中完成，无需上传文件，速度快捷。用户还可以在GitHub上关注该项目。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对一个新推出的网页视频编辑器的功能、性能、用户体验及潜在改进的评价和建议

不同观点：
• zoogeny：赞赏该工具的完成度，并提到目前有很多类似的基于web的视频编辑器，尤其是在ffmpeg WASM移植后涌现。他建议加入生成式AI作为核心功能，以区别于其他工具。
• xnx：提到另一个类似的开源工具（Omniclip），强调该工具的视频不会被发送到未知服务器，注重隐私。
• jony1266：给出用户体验反馈，包括拖放视频、剪辑视频、移动播放头等功能的需求，并提到页面文本选择问题。
• jasonthorsness：对项目的快速响应表示赞赏，但指出时间线自动滚动过于跳动，并建议提供示例剪辑供用户测试。
• 90s_dev：感叹网页视频编辑器的进步，提到过去的难度以及目前主流工具的使用问题，期待使用该工具并研究其源码。
• mncharity：建议在着陆页添加截图，以便用户更快了解工具界面，避免冗长的操作路径。
• koakuma-chan：遇到问题，只能编辑视频的前30秒，而视频总长为23分钟。
• indigodaddy：询问该工具或类似工具是否能简化视频中敏感信息（如密码）的遮盖操作，提到桌面工具的复杂性。
• asadm：建议提供默认项目，让用户无需上传自己的内容即可测试工具。
• Jayakumark：希望支持上传lottie文件，因为remotion支持该格式。
• shkm：对工具的未来发展表示期待，并希望能够用鼠标移动文本。
• dylanjha：建议将该工具作为SDK发布，以便其他应用嵌入使用。
• aaurelions：遇到FFmpeg WASM的进度条问题，指出其在处理过程中可能显得缓慢或无响应。
• higgins：对界面图标是否由AI生成表示好奇。
• s09dfhks：上传剪辑后，预览无法播放。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：部分用户（如koakuma-chan、aaurelions）遇到功能性问题，如视频编辑时长限制和FFmpeg WASM进度条不响应，这可能影响工具的可用性。
• 改进建议：用户普遍对工具的用户体验和功能提出了改进建议，如增加拖放功能、改善时间线操作、提供示例内容和默认项目等。
• 新功能建议：多个用户（如zoogeny、dylanjha）建议加入AI生成视频功能和SDK发布方式，以增强工具的竞争力。
• 隐私关注：xnx提到Omniclip工具的隐私优势，表明用户对数据安全的关注。

data.title: Show HN: Confidential computing for high-assurance RISC-V embedded systems
data.author: mrnoone
data.article_summary: IBM的ACE-RISCV项目是一个开源的机密计算框架，旨在为RISC-V嵌入式系统提供基于虚拟机（VM）的可信执行环境（TEE），重点是形式化验证和可审计的固件。该项目实现了RISC-V CoVE规范的部署模型3，专注于安全监控器的形式化验证，并支持后量子加密（PQC）和本地证明机制。硬件要求包括RISC-V 64位处理器，支持整数（I）、原子（A）、虚拟化（H）等扩展。开发环境需要在Linux系统上配置多种工具和依赖项，如RISC-V工具链、QEMU、OpenSBI和Rust工具链。项目提供了详细的编译和安装指南，支持在SiFive P550开发板上运行机密工作负载。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：RISC-V在安全性、可信计算环境（TEE）以及与CoVE（Confidential Virtual Environments）关系方面的潜力和技术细节。

不同观点：
• [l0ng1nu5] 认为RISC-V目前在通用计算速度上无法与专有架构竞争，但在提供安全保障后，安全意识强的IT管理员会优先选择RISC-V，其他用户会跟随。
• [neom] 关注RISC-V在可信计算领域是否会重蹈x86架构中由于碎片化和不兼容标准导致的开发者体验差和供应商锁定问题，希望通过CoVE和IBM的努力来避免这种情况，并期待在不同TEE架构中实现通用抽象。
• [IshKebab] 询问CoVE与ACE（该代码库）之间的关系，以及在不支持CoVE的P550处理器上如何运行相关功能。
• [hyperhello] 对"有限"网络连接的定义感兴趣，特别是逻辑推理无法支持的边界情况。
• [anonymousDan] 提出与Keystone的区别，质疑RISC-V方案的独特性。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中提到了CoVE和ACE的关系问题，以及如何在不同硬件上实现支持，表明技术实现和兼容性是关注重点。
• neom强调了开发者体验和开放标准的重要性，显示出对RISC-V生态系统健康发展的关注。
• 对"有限"网络连接的讨论反映了对具体技术细节和边界条件的关注，表明用户对实际应用场景的重视。
• 与Keystone的比较显示出用户对不同技术方案之间差异和优势的关注。

争议焦点：RISC-V在可信计算领域的潜力和技术实现细节，特别是在与现有方案（如Keystone）比较时，是否能避免x86遇到的问题并提供更好的开发者体验和开放标准。

Assured Confidential Execution (ACE) for RISC-V
ACE-RISCV is an open-source project, whose goal is to deliver a confidential computing framework with a formally proven security monitor. It is based on the
canonical architecture
and targets RISC-V with the goal of being portable to other architectures. The formal verification efforts focus on the
security monitor implementation
. We invite collaborators to work with us to push the boundaries of provable confidential computing technology.
Formal verification:
This project implements the RISC-V CoVE spec's deployment model 3 referenced in
Appendix D
. The formal specification is embedded in the security monitor's source code and the proofs are in the
verification/
folder. Please read our
paper1
and
paper2
to learn about the approach and goals.
Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) and Attestation
: ACE supports local attestation, a mechanism to authenticate confidential VMs intended for embedded systems with limited or no network connectivity. We already support PQC, specifically we use ML-KEM, SHA-384, and AES-GCM-256 cryptography.
Hardware requirements
We are currently building on RISC-V 64-bit with integer (I), atomic (A) and hypervisor extentions (H), physical memory protection (PMP), memory management unit (MMU), IOPMP, core-local interrupt controller (CLINT), and supervisor timecmp extension (Sstc).
RISC-V hardware to run ACE:
SiFive P550 evaluation board,
see instructions
.
Quick Start
Follow instructions to run one of the sample
confidential workloads
under an
untrusted Linux KVM hypervisor
in an emulated RISC-V environment.
Requirements
Full compilation of the framework takes a long time because many tools are built from sources. Our toolchain currently includes: hypervisor kernel (
Linux kernel
), confidential guest kernel (
Linux kernel
) and firmware (
security monitor
with
OpenSBI firmware
). Make sure to build this project on a machine with at least 4 cores, 4GB RAM, and 50GB disk space for reasonable (~30min) build time.
Dependencies
You must install build dependencies specific to the operating system you use AND install the Rust toolchain. You can also look at the
reproducible build configuration
of the continous integration (CI) system.
Dependencies for Ubuntu 22.04
sudo apt update
# riscv-gnu-toolchain dependencies:
sudo apt -qq -y install autoconf automake autotools-dev curl python3 libmpc-dev libmpfr-dev libgmp-dev gawk build-essential bison flex texinfo gperf libtool patchutils bc zlib1g-dev libexpat-dev xz-utils
# OpenSBI

data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了鸟类在长途迁徙中如何通过其肌肉细胞中的线粒体获得能量。研究表明，迁徙鸟类的线粒体在数量、形状、效率和相互连接方面会发生变化，从而为持续的高强度飞行提供所需的能量。例如，白冠雀和北极燕鸥等鸟类能够飞行数千英里，部分原因是它们的线粒体在特定季节会变得更加高效。这种生理变化是由光周期触发的，而非基因改变，显示了鸟类对环境的高度适应能力。这些发现揭示了线粒体在鸟类迁徙中的关键作用，也展示了生物体如何在不改变遗传基础的情况下适应环境需求。

By
Elizabeth Landau
May 19, 2025
Changes in the number, shape, efficiency and interconnectedness of organelles in the cells of flight muscles provide extra energy for birds’ continent-spanning feats.

How do small birds migrate long distances? Mitochondria are key.
Nan Cao for
Quanta Magazine
Introduction
By
Elizabeth Landau
Contributing Writer
May 19, 2025
View PDF/Print Mode

W
eighing in at a single ounce, the white-crowned sparrow can fly 2,600 miles, from Mexico to Alaska, on its annual spring migration, sometimes traveling 300 miles in a single night. Arctic terns make even longer journeys of 10,000 miles and more from the Arctic Circle to Antarctica, while great snipes fly over food-poor deserts and seas, sometimes covering 4,200 miles in four days without stopping.
During migration season, many bird species become continent-spanning, high-endurance athletes. “They’re flapping their wings several times a second for up to eight hours at a time,” said
Soren Coulson
, who studies migration physiology at the University of Memphis. For humans, an equivalent feat — say, running nonstop without food, water or rest for days at a time — would be unimaginable.
“We were just amazed and interested in how can these birds fly for thousands of miles without stopping, at a really high intensity, when most of us can barely run a 5K,” said
Paulo Mesquita
, who studies mitochondrial physiology and muscle aging at the Oklahoma Medical Research Foundation.
Scientists have long been fascinated with the
physiological changes
that birds undergo before and during migration. Some birds eat so much fat before their journeys that they double in body weight. In some species, their hearts are enlarged to pump more blood, or their digestive tracts grow and then shrink. But researchers have only recently started to explore at a fundamental level how migratory birds get the energy required to keep themselves aloft for days on end without eating.
Last year, two independent groups published research that explored migratory bird physiology in the lab and field to probe what happens at the subcellular level that allows birds to cover vast distances. They both found answers in biology’s most fundamental engine: mitochondria.
Their studies show how small changes in the number, shape, efficiency and interconnectedness of mitochondria can have huge physiological consequences that contribute to birds’ long-duration, continent-spanning flights.
“Exercise physiologists study the mitochondria because they provide the energy needed to maintain healthy cells, to maintain proper cellular function — but also, just in general, the energy we need to exercise,” Mesquita said. “That energy is what fuels movement.”

To Paulo Mesquita, an exercise physiologist, mitochondria are the center of the universe.
Courtesy of Paulo Mesquita/OMRF
These pioneering studies on mitochondrial performance and bird migration highlight the fact that a seasonal response to changing light levels, not physical preparation, triggers crucial subcellular changes, said
Wendy Hood
, who studies physiological ecology at Auburn University in Alabama; Mesquita worked with her and other colleagues on these questions during his graduate studies.
Humans “have to train for a while before we start to see any changes in the performance of our mitochondria,” she said. With migratory birds, “it’s spring, they get the right light cycles, and their body starts producing more and better, or higher-quality, mitochondria.”
The recent work advances the idea that there are significant ways in which an organism can change, without modifying its underlying genetic makeup, in response to its environment, said
Scott McWilliams
, a professor of wildlife ecology and physiology at the University of Rhode Island who was not involved in either study. This “phenotypic flexibility” in birds has been shown to vary according to seasons and population, and these studies are some of the first to demonstrate this across species and subspecies at the mitochondrial level.
“Such a theme,” he said, “is centrally important for understanding how birds during migration accomplish their athletic feats.”

data.title: Faster Firewalls with Bpfilter
data.author: signa11
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了网络流量过滤工具的演变和性能改进，尤其是bpfilter项目的引入。传统上，iptables是标准的包过滤工具，但其性能逐渐无法满足需求，因而被nftables取代。nftables通过将规则翻译成Netfilter字节码来提高效率。然而，BPF（Berkeley Packet Filter）提供了更高的灵活性和性能优势，允许更高效的包过滤。

bpfilter项目旨在结合nftables的易用性和BPF的性能优势，通过在用户空间将iptables规则转换为BPF程序来提升性能。bpfilter包含三个主要组件：bpfilter守护进程、libbpfilter库和命令行工具bfcli。用户通过bfcli定义过滤规则，规则被发送到守护进程以生成和执行BPF程序。

尽管bpfilter可以通过iptables接口使用，但目前仅支持一些基本功能，如IPv4地址和协议字段过滤，模块功能尚未支持。总体而言，bpfilter为需要高效网络过滤的专业环境提供了一个有潜力的解决方案。
